executive_preview: The clearest industry shift this week is toward more selective electrification rather than a uniform EV push. Ford is preparing a lower-cost electric pickup around manufacturing simplification, drivetrain efficiency and a smaller battery, while GM is reallocating plant capacity toward hybrids and Rivian is expanding electric commercial-van capability. Used-EV data also shows improving prices and faster turnover, but performance varies sharply by model.

lead_development.title: Vehicle software is becoming a service, repair and safety constraint.
lead_development.what_happened: A reported Tesla battery replacement required extensive firmware and controller work, automotive cybersecurity research identified 413 reported vulnerabilities and 827 vulnerable libraries, and Tesla is using Turo to expose more renters to supervised Full Self-Driving.
lead_development.why_it_matters: Software now affects repairability, cybersecurity, monetization and customer access. Independent repairers need diagnostic and authorization capabilities that go beyond conventional mechanical skills, while manufacturers face pressure to secure connected systems and support long-term serviceability.

signals.title: Ford's Fathom EV Strategy Centers on Cost, Manufacturing and Digital Upsell
signals.teaser: Ford has produced more than 5,000 large aluminum castings for its upcoming Fathom electric pickup and says approximately 90% of validation testing is complete.

signals.title: GM Repositions Three-Row SUV Capacity Toward Hybrids
signals.teaser: GM is preparing Lansing Delta Township for potential hybrid versions of the Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse and GMC Acadia as part of more than $2 billion in planned regional investment.

signals.title: Rivian Expands Electric Commercial-Van Utility Beyond Urban Routes
signals.teaser: Rivian has begun delivering commercial vans with a larger 129-kWh LFP battery and a dual-motor all-wheel-drive option.

downside.title: Affordable EV launch execution may be constrained by supplier quality and production-rate problems.
downside.teaser: Ford identified supply-base readiness as the principal outstanding Fathom risk while still completing validation.

upside.title: Use model-level used-EV data to expand profitable retail inventory selectively.
upside.teaser: Used EVs showed faster average turns and stronger price gains, but performance varied widely by model.
